parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: One atom of each of the four elements $\text{H}$, $\text{C}$, $\text{N}$ and $\text{O}$ can bond together in different ways. Two examples are molecules of cyanic acid, $\text{HOCN}$, and isocyanic acid, $\text{HNCO}$. The atoms are bonded in the order they are written.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text:
Draw 'dot-and-cross' diagrams of these two acids, showing outer shell electrons only.
$\text{HOCN}$, cyanic acid
$\text{HNCO}$, isocyanic acid

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest the values of the bond angles $\text{HNC}$ and $\text{NCO}$ in isocyanic acid.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Suggest which acid, cyanic or isocyanic, will have the shorter $\text{C-N}$ bond length. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Isocyanic acid is a weak acid.
$$\text{HNCO} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^{+} + \text{NCO}^{-} \qquad K_{\text{a}} = 1.2 \times 10^{-4}\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$$

Calculate the pH of a $0.10\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ solution of isocyanic acid.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Sodium cyanate, $\text{NaNCO}$, is used in the production of isocyanic acid. Sodium cyanate is prepared commercially by reacting urea, $(\text{NH}_2)_2\text{CO}$, with sodium carbonate. Other products in this reaction are carbon dioxide, ammonia and steam.

Write an equation for the production of $\text{NaNCO}$ by this method.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Barium hydroxide, $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$, is completely ionised in aqueous solutions. During the addition of $30.0\text{ cm}^{3}$ of $0.100\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ to $20.0\text{ cm}^{3}$ of $0.100\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ isocyanic acid, the pH was measured.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the $[\text{OH}^{-}]$ at the end of the addition.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Use your value in (i) to calculate $[\text{H}^{+}]$ and the pH of the solution at the end of the addition.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
On the following axes, sketch how the pH changes during the addition of a total of $30.0\text{ cm}^{3}$ of $0.100\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ to $20.0\text{ cm}^{3}$ of $0.100\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ isocyanic acid.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: The cyanate ion, $\text{NCO}^{-}$, can act as a monodentate ligand.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: State what is meant by the terms

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.stem: Silver ions, $\text{Ag}^{+}$, react with cyanate ions to form a linear complex.
parts.text: Suggest the formula of this complex, including its charge.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem:
When heated with $\text{HCl}\text{(aq)}$, organic isocyanates, $\text{RNCO}$, are hydrolysed to the amine salt, $\text{RNH}_3\text{Cl}$, and $\text{CO}_2$.
$$\text{RNCO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{RNH}_3\text{Cl} + \text{CO}_2$$

A $1.00\text{ g}$ sample of an organic isocyanate, $\text{RNCO}$, was treated in this way, and the $\text{CO}_2$ produced was absorbed in an excess of aqueous $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ according to the equation shown. The solid $\text{BaCO}_3$ precipitated weighed $1.66\text{ g}$.
$$\text{Ba(OH)}_2\text{(aq)} + \text{CO}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{BaCO}_3\text{(s)} + \text{H}_2\text{O(l)}$$

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of $\text{BaCO}_3$ produced.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text: Hence calculate the $M_{r}$ of the organic isocyanate $\text{RNCO}$.

parts.label: (e)(iii)
parts.stem: The R group in $\text{RNCO}$ and $\text{RNH}_3\text{Cl}$ contains carbon and hydrogen only.
parts.text: Use your $M_{r}$ value calculated in (ii) to suggest the molecular formula of the organic isocyanate $\text{RNCO}$.

parts.label: (e)(iv)
parts.text:
Suggest a possible structure of the amine $\text{RNH}_2$, which forms the amine salt, $\text{RNH}_3\text{Cl}$.

{{figure:pdf_visual_03.png}}
